items.reason: Lift flows from the preset through build options into row ordering and marking.

The pin alias sets Lift without spelling-related warnings or findings.
Reading lift after pin gives lift precedence.
An undeclared grant remains false.
Both keys record nonfatal type findings.
Derived-ordering identifiers, comments, and test filenames are renamed; alias references remain explicit.
Manual and unrelated pin mechanisms are unchanged.
The field tag, description, and shipped grant use lift.
Repository attribution reaches bound sets from sibling worktrees, with integration coverage.
Checkout attribution returns before the repository pass and preserves existing ranking.
Task-set tags retain first-pass precedence, with regression coverage.
Repository indexing includes both bound and unbound Task sets.
Repository attribution indexes and matches RepoCommonDir.
Cursor keys still combine project name and identifier, so collisions can lift another repository’s row.
Missing or unknown repository identities produce no attribution or user-facing message.
The repository pass concatenates all answering kinds, explicitly tested with two kinds.
Launch captures repository identity once; a counting git test checks three rebuilds.
Status builds use empty pane facts and have coverage for no attribution git calls.
Lifting operates on already-filtered rows and does not widen the preset.
Repository Maps are attributed while existing visibility rules exclude abandoned, broken, and archived Maps under active.
Repository answers concatenate Task sets before Maps, with combined-kind coverage.
Map session stamps return before repository attribution, with regression coverage.
Routines implement no locality attribution, and a comment explicitly explains why.

scores.rationale: Clear seams and substantial regression coverage, but repository identity collisions remain untested and Map attribution ignores ascending preset order.
